clue.text: I waged wars, crossing line, one over the mountain

indicators.note: the scrambled letters run across the line, sitting between its two letters

parts.note: RY, short for railway, is a standard crossword line

indicators.note: waged wars suggests turmoil, so the letters of I waged are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A warrior boasts of the campaigns he fought, crossing a frontier and going over a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wars' is an unusual anagram signal, read as turmoil; 'crossing' has the scrambled letters span the line, RY being railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridgeway is an old track running along high ground, so it is one route over the hills.

clue.text: Take away antique from Nile, so excited

definitions.note: an archaic verb meaning to remove or carry off; antique flags the old word

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up, so Nile and so are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be removing an ancient artefact from the banks of the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'antique' is part of the definition, telling you the verb is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an obsolete legal verb for removing or withdrawing something, hence the archaism label.

clue.text: Consummate in this location, transformed by Henry Moore? Not so!

indicators.note: transformed means changed in shape, so the letters of the sculptor's name and the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An art critic suggests a famous sculptor reshaped something, then retracts the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges HENRY MOORE plus NOT SO; 'by' just joins them. Henry Moore was a British sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Newlyweds traditionally consummate their marriage on holiday at a getaway destination for couples.

clue.text: Cracking basket-maker performed satire

indicators.note: one piece cracking another breaks into it, so it sits inside

parts.note: cane is woven to make baskets
performed means did

explanation.surface: A splendid satire performed by someone who weaves baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like praise for the satire but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's novella is a famous satirical work mocking philosophical optimism.

clue.text: When we hear the news, I'm afraid Nestor and I crack up about problem child

parts.note: News at Ten is a British evening television bulletin, so the news comes at ten

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go around the exclamation
to crack up is to break apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: Someone frightened as the evening news airs, watching a breakdown with a friend named Nestor.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a long-running British TV news programme, so the news comes 'at ten'. 'crack up' scrambles the pair into TIONSER, which 'about' wraps around the cry of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult child often misbehaves to get noticed, the classic description of a show-off craving notice.

clue.text: Its cargo is loaded at the other end?

definitions.text: Its cargo is loaded at the other end?

indicators.note: cargo that is loaded is shifted about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shipping query about a freighter whose cargo is taken aboard at its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' rearranges ITS CARGO; the whole clue is also a saucy hint at a climax 'at the other end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes climactic sexual release, which the clue hints at with innuendo about loading.

clue.text: Daughter wearing one ring on another pleasure boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
the bells' peal wears the daughter, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
another ring, here the round letter O

explanation.surface: A daughter wearing a ring stacked on another one, aboard a pleasure boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts D inside PEAL; 'on' puts that above O, the second ring, in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small pedal-powered craft hired for fun on lakes at resorts.

clue.text: Migrants told to return almost left a …

indicators.note: returning means the word for told is written backwards

parts.note: told means said

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Displaced people are ordered home after nearly departing, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns SAID into DIAS; 'almost' cuts PORT to POR.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a people scattered from their homeland, a collective term for dispersed emigrants.

clue.text: See 16
… region to rebuild bypass

indicators.note: rebuilding the word region reassembles its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: an area being redeveloped with a new ring road.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass a matter is to disregard it, a figurative use of going around something.

clue.text: Long time, a week to fill, gradually disappeared

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it

indicators.note: the a and the week fill the time period, going inside it

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone with a whole week to fill finds time dragging until it fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' puts A and W inside DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounds or feelings that fade out slowly are said to have petered out, the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: Actress and comedienne's part doing Wyndham's

indicators.note: a part of the words doing Wyndham's holds the name

explanation.surface: A performer is playing a role at Wyndham's, a West End theatre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Wyndham's is a London West End theatre, which makes the surface about stage acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell Gwyn was a Restoration stage performer famous for comic roles and as Charles II's mistress.

clue.text: What's prescribed's not cocaine, taking time for serious thought

indicators.note: not cocaine means that letter goes out of the word for prescribed drugs
taking time for it means the time letter comes in where the drug was

parts.note: medication is what a doctor prescribes
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription excludes cocaine, and the patient needs time to think hard about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the C from MEDICATION and 'taking ... for' puts T in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep contemplation or focused reflection is the core sense of this word, as in religious practice.

clue.text: Hypocrisy, MP to MP — could be a problem here

indicators.note: here points to the letters right in front of the solver, where the word lies across the run

explanation.surface: Politicians accusing each other of double standards suggests something wrong in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The word spans the end of 'Hypocrisy' and the following 'MP to MP'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or indication that something is wrong, like a fever pointing to an illness.

clue.text: Go round impersonating French where they won't have the foggiest, like? +

indicators.note: go round means the word for go surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: go means energy, pep
impersonating someone is acting as them
ou is French for where
the suffix -y means like or having the quality of

explanation.surface: Someone playing a French character goes round clueless, not having the faintest idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' means energy here, not travel, and 'like' is the adjective ending -Y. 'the foggiest' plays on the idiom for having no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick yellowish London fog was called a pea-souper, so the adjective describes dense, visibility-killing murk.

clue.text: Cook's gone off Prior, perhaps after match — he's joined the opposition!

indicators.note: after places the keeper piece behind the match piece

parts.note: someone who poaches eggs or fish is a cook
milk that has gone off has turned
a match is a game
Matt Prior was England's wicketkeeper, so he exemplifies a keeper

explanation.surface: England cricketer Alastair Cook gets annoyed with teammate Matt Prior after a match, as if he has switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook and Prior were both England cricketers; Prior was the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who switches sides, now protecting what they once attacked.

clue.text: Setter's thrown up nuts and cheese

indicators.note: in a down answer, thrown up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
nuts means crazy, mental

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler has been sick after eating nuts and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' turns ME upwards to give EM in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Swiss hard variety with large holes, made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Thorough, working for Section No 8?

parts.note: in means operating or working, as with a machine that is on
dept, short for department, is a section of an organisation
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone employed in Section 8 of an office has to be meticulous.
explanation.walkthrough: H counts as number 8 because it is the eighth letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is comprehensive and detailed, examining every aspect fully.

clue.text: Get out of line, end of holiday being delayed by a Boojum's return

indicators.note: end of holiday names the final letter of the holiday word as the one to shift
delaying a letter makes it arrive later in the word

parts.note: a break is a short holiday

indicators.note: return means the creature's name is read backwards

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's poem a Boojum is a particularly dangerous kind of Snark

explanation.surface: A holiday's last day is postponed by a strange creature returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's poem a Boojum is a kind of Snark. Reversed it gives KRANS; joining that to the holiday word doubles the K, and 'being delayed' shifts the first K later, between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers leaving formation step out of their row, figuratively meaning to defy the group.

clue.text: Double Gloucester in German houses? +

indicators.note: German houses means the run of words is holding the answer within it

explanation.surface: Double Gloucester, an English cheese, is served in German homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Gloucester' (a hard English cheese) splits: 'Double' is the definition, and 'houses' shows the answer is held across 'Gloucester in German'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is a dead ringer, someone almost identical to another person.

clue.text: See 16
21A 24's hound and horse keeping loose

indicators.note: the horse keeps the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse
to loose a knot is to undo it

explanation.surface: A countryside worker's dog and horse are kept from running free.
explanation.walkthrough: 21A and 24 together make GAMEKEEPER, from the linked answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever or pointer trained to find shot birds works alongside the man who manages shooting estates.

clue.text: Filling of form for enclosure by closing date: he eventually gets cheque

indicators.note: the filling is enclosed by the pieces around it

parts.note: the closing of something is its end
to date someone is to see them

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for completing a form with an enclosure before the closing date, after which someone gets paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' is a verb here, to go out with someone; 'for enclosure by' sets the form's filling between the two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A person to whom a cheque is signed over by endorsement eventually receives its value.

clue.text: Muses retrogressively about laevo-rotatory circular current

indicators.note: about means surrounding the left-handed letter
going backwards, so the number of Muses is written in reverse

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth
laevo means left, so L
the circular letter is O

explanation.surface: A scientific description of a rotating ocean current, phrased in learned jargon about the Muses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrogressively' turns NINE into ENIN, and 'about' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific warm-water phenomenon is an ocean current that disrupts weather worldwide.

clue.text: See 16
72 at Muirfield, as champ not taking a drop +

definitions.meaning: Muirfield is a Scottish championship golf course; 72 could be a round's score from the tees

definitions.text: as champ not taking a drop
definitions.meaning: a champion abstainer never takes a drop of alcohol

explanation.surface: A golfer shoots 72 at Muirfield, the Open champion refusing a penalty drop.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a drop is a free or penalty re-placing of the ball; here it means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol is described this way; the first reading splits it as a golfing sum.
